code:
$ ssh deploy@203.0.113.10
deploy@203.0.113.10's password:

# everything typed and returned travels encrypted
# SSH listens on port 22 by default
caption: ssh user@host gets you a command-line session on a remote server.

steps.label: Private key
steps.sub: id_ed25519 — stays on your machine, never shared

steps.label: Public key
steps.sub: id_ed25519.pub — safe to copy onto any server

code:
$ ssh-copy-id deploy@203.0.113.10

# puts your public key in, on the server:
~/.ssh/authorized_keys

$ chmod 700 ~/.ssh
$ chmod 600 ~/.ssh/authorized_keys
caption: SSH refuses an authorized_keys file with loose permissions — chmod is required.

steps.label: Nothing to intercept
steps.sub: no secret is ever transmitted over the network

steps.label: Instant revoke
steps.sub: delete one line from authorized_keys to cut off access

subtitle: What to check first when something breaks
